key_agent_trends: A subscriber class action treats frontier-lab slowdown talk as an antitrust pact, putting safety coordination in court.
Labs are publishing how much of their own R&D agents now lead, with Anthropic at 26% AL4 and 30,000 internal agents.
Discovery agents are being taught to replay past search trees instead of paying for every new rollout.
Long-form media is shipping multi-agent writers with persistent world memory rather than single-prompt generators.
Banks are treating agent identity as a KYC problem as card networks push Know-Your-Agent rails.

stories.headline: Class action says labs made an illegal AI slowdown pact
stories.what_happened: On 19 September 2026 a proposed class action was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. It names Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI (styled SpaceXAI in some coverage) and argues that public agreement after Dario Amodei’s 12 September essay to slow frontier development violated antitrust law by reducing the value of paid subscriptions. The complaint is brought for ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Gemini subscribers. The companies did not immediately comment. The filing alleges coordination; it does not prove a binding agreement.
stories.why_it_matters: Safety talks among rivals now have a litigation tax. Labs that coordinate on pace or standards will treat counsel and antitrust waivers as part of the product roadmap.

stories.headline: Anthropic says Claude leads 26% of its own AI R&D
stories.what_happened: Anthropic published an R&D Automation Index showing that as of August 2026 Claude ‘leads’ (Epoch AL4) 26% of the lab’s AI research and development work, up from under 1% in February. More than 90% of that work is at AL3 or above. No measured subset is fully autonomous (AL5). About 30,000 agents ran on its main internal platform at once; monitors blocked 0.002% of more than 1 billion August decisions. The figures are self-reported.
stories.why_it_matters: A frontier lab is now quantifying how close agents are to building the next model. That is the public scoreboard for recursive self-improvement, even if third parties have not audited it.

stories.headline: Dream-RSI lets discovery agents replay past searches
stories.what_happened: Google, DeepMind, Maryland and Virginia researchers published Dream-RSI, which turns prior discovery trees into a replay simulator so an agent can test new search policies without re-running expensive rollouts. The coding model stays fixed; only the exploration policy changes. On Gemini 3.1 Pro, Lasso-path work dropped from 550 to 317 attempts and beat sklearn and glmnet on six datasets. Versus SimpleTES the paper reports up to 162x fewer discovery-agent calls. Coverage on 19 September brought the preprint into the daily cycle.
stories.why_it_matters: Self-improving agents are bottlenecked by repeat evaluation cost. Replaying history is a cheaper loop than spawning more live agents.

stories.headline: Pocket FM launches Sherpa multi-agent fiction platform
stories.what_happened: On 19 September 2026 Pocket FM launched Sherpa, a writing platform that uses separate agents for ideation, planning, research, prose and review plus a Narrative World Model that stores characters, relationships and events across hundreds of episodes. The company says models are trained on its catalogue of more than 770,000 titles, 550,000 creators and 5.5 billion hours of play. It positions the stack as studio-scale continuity for a single creator, not one-shot generation.
stories.why_it_matters: Agent memory is moving from chat context into a persistent world model for products that must stay consistent over long horizons.

stories.headline: Banks face a Know-Your-Agent payments problem
stories.what_happened: Fortune reported on 19 September 2026 that banks must identify who an AI agent is acting for when it shops or pays. Ant International is working with Visa and Mastercard on a Know-Your-Agent interoperability layer so card networks, wallets and marketplaces can recognise trusted agents without a new signup on every rail. Each agent is meant to map to a validated operator or cardholder, with ongoing behavioural checks. The underlying collaboration was announced earlier in September; the 19 September coverage frames it as a bank compliance issue.
stories.why_it_matters: Agentic commerce stalls if merchants cannot tell a trusted agent from a rogue script. Identity rails are becoming as important as the checkout protocol.
